scope.title: Fillet and chamfer feature parity audit
scope.baseline: OCCT V7_9_3 source inventory plus the recorded Truck/Pieza revisions. Includes 3D, 2D, related workflows and all textual candidates under the discovery rules.
scope.meaning_of_all: Every dedicated test-grid entry, matching registered test/helper, discovered blend command and retained reference in this pinned checkout. This is not a claim about all mathematical configurations or current/future OCCT releases.
scope.execution: All 1,026 inventoried entries have recorded native OCCT harness attempts. Separately, 156 passing entries were instrumented; 148 invoked blend, producing 161 capture attempts and 160 Truck replay attempts. Captured replay separates import, selection, unsupported intent, construction, panic/timeout, mesh and sampled STEP outcomes. Source/artifact hashes are checked. Every case-level full parity verdict remains unverified; independent paired probes and targeted regressions supply additional capability evidence.
scope.mapping: Capability assessments describe observable outcomes supported or restricted by reviewed source evidence. Per-case tags and links are automated hints; they do not prove Truck handles that fixture.
scope.objective: Achieve at least OCCT-level fillet/chamfer capabilities and robustness for equivalent modeling tasks in Truck/Pieza.
scope.equivalence: Judge the requested geometry, dimensions, validity, editing behavior and practical performance. Different APIs, algorithms, languages, surface representations and internal operation sequences are acceptable. Missing a corresponding OCCT method is not evidence of a feature gap.

status_definitions.implemented-with-tests: The stated capability has an implementation and relevant assertions, through any equivalent construction. Executed checks are recorded separately where available; broader OCCT case parity remains unverified.
status_definitions.partial: Some configurations have supporting evidence; others have known restrictions or remain unverified. Read the outcome and scope before treating any specific case as a gap.
status_definitions.behavior-difference: The inspected constructions produce different physical constraints or behavior for the same nominal input. Check whether parameter conversion or another existing route provides equivalent results before declaring a capability gap.
status_definitions.app-limitation: An observed product restriction prevents expressing or using a capability. An internal pipeline difference alone is not sufficient evidence.
status_definitions.unverified: The requested outcome has not been established from the inspected evidence. Absence of an OCCT-style API does not establish lack of capability.
status_definitions.reference-only: An OCCT implementation choice retained for investigation. It is not itself a feature requirement or parity deficit.

validation_contract: Express each case as a modeling task: input geometry, physical selection, intended radius/distances/angle, termination and expected result. Identify the same physical entities without relying on ordinal edge IDs across kernels.

Accept any Truck/Pieza construction that satisfies the task, including parameter conversion and composed operations. Require equivalent editing intent and automation; a manually sculpted lookalike does not establish a parametric feature.

API names, signatures, call counts, solver strategy, patch representation and face counts are not parity requirements. Internal differences matter only through observable correctness, robustness, editing or performance.
Record operation failure, crash/timeout, invalid output and valid output separately. A harness expected failure is not a working blend; successful return alone is not proof of correctness.

Validate contact radius/distances/angle, tangency where required, orientation, closed topology/mesh, material membership and global self-intersection independently. Check open-shell tasks against their own boundary contract.
Compare shape and dimensions within explicit tolerances, with volume as a supplementary check. Different valid topology decompositions are acceptable.

Preserve unchanged input on failure; verify persistent selections after upstream edits, STEP round trips and downstream modeling. These outcomes do not require matching OCCT history or diagnostic methods.
Use analytic expectations where available; OCCT supplies cases and comparative evidence, not an infallible oracle or a ceiling on supported behavior.
Record versions, tolerances, physical selection, runtime and fixture hash with results. Practical latency matters, but matching OCCT timing exactly is not required.
